query_analysis.original_query: Calculate the theoretical minimum energy required to separate a binary gas-liquid mixture under isothermal conditions. The feed stream contains 60 mol% Component A and 40 mol% Component B, entering at a pressure of 5 bar and a temperature of 298 K. The desired products are a gas stream with 95 mol% Component A and a liquid stream with 90 mol% Component B. Assume ideal gas and liquid behavior, and neglect heat losses or inefficiencies in the separation process.
query_analysis.expanded_query: Determine the theoretical minimum work required for an isothermal separation of a binary mixture, given a feed of 60 mol% Component A and 40 mol% Component B at 5 bar and 298 K, into a gas stream of 95 mol% Component A and a liquid stream of 90 mol% Component B, assuming ideal gas and liquid behavior and neglecting inefficiencies.

clarification_questions: Are there any specific thermodynamic models that should be used, other than ideal behavior?
Is there any information available about the vapor pressure of the components at the given temperature?
